```{python}
# Molly section

# grid construction reference: https://james-brennan.github.io/posts/fast_gridding_geopandas/

def grid_bin(df, proj='EPSG:4326'):
  # take in df with features "latitude" (ranging 31 to 37) and "longitude" (ranging -109 to -115) and return geodataframe with a new column that is the grid number

  # Create geometry feature of input df
  df['geometry'] = gpd.points_from_xy(df.longitude, df.latitude,
    crs=proj)
  gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(data=df, geometry='geometry')

  # Initialize grid dataframe
  xmin = -114.5   # total area for the grid with ranging values
  ymin = 31.2     # describing latitude and longitude limits for AZ
  xmax = -109
  ymax = 37

  num_x = 15  # how many cells in x direction minus 1
  num_y = 20  # how many cells in y direction minus 1
              # total cells is num_x*num_y (336 in our case)

  cell_size_x = (xmax-xmin)/num_x   # how many cells across and down
  cell_size_y = (ymax-ymin)/num_y

  # projection of the grid
  crs = proj

  grid_cells = []
  for x0 in np.arange(xmin, xmax+cell_size_x, cell_size_x ):
      for y0 in np.arange(ymin, ymax+cell_size_y, cell_size_y):
          # bounds
          x1 = x0-cell_size_x
          y1 = y0+cell_size_y
          grid_cells.append( shapely.geometry.box(x0, y0, x1, y1)  )

  grid = gpd.GeoDataFrame(grid_cells, columns=['geometry'], 
                                 crs=crs)

  # print(grid.shape)   # axis 0 is the number of cells in the grid

  # Spatially join (sjoin) input df and grid
  gdf_joined = gpd.sjoin(left_df=gdf, right_df=grid, how='left')

  # Rename column to be more intuitive
  gdf_joined['gridspace'] = gdf_joined['index_right']
  gdf_joined = gdf_joined.drop(['index_right'], axis=1)

  return gdf_joined
```
